## Overview

IMC Calculadora is a YMYL health tool, not a marketing site. The direction reads as a precise instrument a person can trust with a health question: calm, symmetric, mostly static, with the calculated number itself treated as the hero content wherever it appears.

## Colors

Cool off-white ground (#F4F6F5) and white surface (#FFFFFF), charcoal ink with a cool undertone (#1A2421), one locked accent: deep teal (#0E5C52), used for the calculate button and any single primary action per view. A muted slate-blue support color (#3B5B6D) exists for secondary UI (links inside body text, secondary badges) but never competes with the teal for primary attention. A hairline border color (#DCE3E1) replaces shadows for most separation.

A declared categorical scale (six steps, scale-bajopeso through scale-obesidad3) is reserved specifically for BMI/IOM category displays — the color-coded table rows and result badges already planned for the site's content. These colors are never repeated as decorative page elements outside that specific use.

## Typography

Headings in Space Grotesk (weight 600), tight leading near 1.05-1.1 even at large sizes. Body in IBM Plex Sans (weight 400), comfortable leading, body copy measured to roughly 65 characters wide. The one place type gets dramatically large is a calculated result (the IMC number, a weight range, a percentile) — treat that number the way a headline treats a word: it can be the single largest element on the page.

## Layout

Low variance (0.2): symmetric, centered, institutional composition. No off-center breakout heroes, no overlapping tilted images. This is a deliberate choice for a medical tool — calm and predictable reads as more trustworthy here than dynamic asymmetry. The calculator widget itself is the one "hero" element per page: centered, prominent, with generous surrounding whitespace.

## Elevation & Depth

Elevation is reserved for exactly one component: the calculator widget, which gets a hairline border plus a very subtle ground-tinted shadow so it reads as a distinct "instrument panel" sitting on the page. Every other separation (between FAQ items, table rows, sections) uses hairline dividers or spacing, never a card shadow.

## Shapes

Corner radius is small and consistent: 2px on small elements (badges, inputs), 6px on larger containers (the calculator panel, buttons). Nothing pill-shaped, nothing sharp-square elsewhere — one restrained scale held everywhere.

## Components

- **Buttons**: solid teal, 6px radius, no shadow, sentence case (never uppercase), one label per intent ("Calcular" is the only calculate-action label anywhere on the site).
- **Calculator widget**: the one card/panel component on the site. Hairline border, minimal shadow, generous internal padding, the result number rendered at display scale within it.
- **Inputs**: flat, bordered (#DCE3E1), teal focus ring on focus, large touch targets (minimum 44px height) for mobile.
- **Category scale swatches**: small square or pill swatches (not full-row backgrounds) paired with the category label, using the six declared scale colors consistently across every page that shows a BMI or weight-gain category table.
- **FAQ / accordion**: hairline dividers between items, no card wrapper.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do's
- Do treat the calculated result number as the largest, boldest element on any page that shows one.
- Do keep every hero and section symmetric and calm — this is a trust-first medical tool, not a marketing landing page.
- Do use hairline dividers between FAQ items, table rows, and list content instead of card shadows.
- Do reserve the teal accent for exactly one primary action per view.
- Do use flat, bordered inputs with a visible teal focus ring for accessibility.
- Do keep the six-step category scale visually consistent everywhere it appears (homepage, imc-ninos, imc-embarazo, metodologia).

### Don'ts
- Never use a card shadow to fake hierarchy anywhere except the calculator widget itself.
- Never mix warm and cool greys — neutrals stay cool-toned throughout.
- Never add decorative icons that don't map to real content (no generic checkmark/lightbulb icon rows).
- Don't apply the teal accent to more than one interactive element per section.
- Never let the category-scale colors drift or get reused for unrelated decoration.
- Never use uppercase eyebrow labels above headings — the section's place on the page already says what it is.
